summary: Configured persistent rsyslog forwarding for `inventory` messages from node2 to node1 over TCP. Messages are stored at `/var/log/inventory/node2.log`. Both nodes were restarted sequentially; boot identities changed, services recovered, and forwarding remained operational. CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were retained.
actions_performed: Configured node1 to receive TCP syslog on port 514 and persist node2 `inventory` messages.
Added a persistent firewalld rule for TCP/514.
Configured node2 with an on-disk queue, infinite retries, and shutdown persistence.
Validated both rsyslog configurations and enabled service startup.
Verified live delivery, queued delivery while node1 restarted, and fresh delivery after node2 restarted.
Safely restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Forward inventory logs from node2 and persist them under /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
evidence.summary: Shows the collector listener/firewall configuration, sender rule, emitted marker, and matching records in the required file.
Configuration validation succeeds; node2 uses TCP with an on-disk linked-list queue, infinite retries, and save-on-shutdown.
Boot ID changed from 05c54227-09be-48f2-b315-751cff5f7dca to 73d110b2-ed75-4160-9173-071ff14787fc. The listener, firewall rule, existing data, and a message queued during downtime all recovered.
Boot ID changed from 71f12f87-337d-4ff3-b414-9680244c2694 to e58370f6-9a66-46e9-a750-f5ebf42b25d5. rsyslog recovered, re-established TCP forwarding, and delivered a new post-restart message.

evidence.requirement: Retain installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before and after configuration and restarts.
